text:
zoe-peopleops: Heads up — Dan submitted a promotion for Alex (L4->L5) but requested an effective date of 2026-06-01 even though Lattice approval went through 2026-07-01. Manager wants retro to align with project milestone and is asking for a retro > 30 days. Need process for exception memo + tax handling (Alex is UK-based). :exclamation:

dan-eng-manager: short version: team agreed contributions started June 1 and comp budget was allocated for June. I approved quickly in July and missed the effective date. Can we grant retro back to June 1?

omar-comp: Retro >30 days requires Comp Director + Legal sign-off (per playbook). For UK employees we also need to consider PAYE reporting and potential employee tax code adjustments. Also: any retro beyond 90 days triggers a formal Exec exception review.

jess-payroll: Payroll timeline: next major run 2026-07-20 18:00 UTC, cutoff 2026-07-18 23:59 UTC. If approved we can include retro in July run; if paperwork arrives after cutoff it will be manual adj. For UK we will coordinate with tax team to confirm month of tax reporting.

tax-uk: FYI: PAYE rules — if retro income is processed in a later tax month, it may need coding notice adjustments and could change employee take-home pay unexpectedly. We recommend offering a net-of-tax gross-up conversation if the retro causes significant tax increases for the employee.

dan-eng-manager: sounds reasonable. What exact docs do you need for Comp Director + Legal? I can draft an exception memo.

omar-comp: Required: 1) Manager exception memo (signed) with explicit effective date and justification, 2) Lattice snapshot showing original approval timestamp, 3) Comp Director approval email, 4) Legal confirmation on employment/tax treatment, 5) Payroll ticket before cutoff. Memo should include a short business justification and budget owner sign-off.

zoe-peopleops: Draft memo template (paste, edit, send):

```
Subject: Exception request — Retroactive promotion effective 2026-06-01 for Alex (EMPID 44521)

I, Dan [last], request an exception to set the promotion effective date to 2026-06-01 despite Lattice approval completed on 2026-07-01. Business justification: core project milestone delivered starting 2026-06-01; budget was approved in Q2 forecast and owner confirmed funds are available. Requested compensation change: base salary from  98,000 ->  110,000. Retro period: 2026-06-01 through 2026-06-30. I acknowledge comp director and legal review required for retro > 30 days.

Manager signature: Dan [last]
Budget owner signature: Priya [last]
Date: 2026-07-02
```

zoe-peopleops: After sending memo, open payroll ticket with subject "EXCEPTION-BACKPAY - Alex 44521 - effective 2026-06-01" and attach the memo + Lattice snapshot. Tag @omar-comp and @tax-uk.

lattice-bot: Lattice snapshot requested — attach approval history and proposed effective-date change. Note: editing approved records may be restricted; use exception flow.

jess-payroll: Once ticket is filed we'll draft a gross/net estimate. If the gross-up is requested we need comp sign-off on payment source (manager budget vs central comp pool). Gross-ups need Legal review for employment contract language in UK locale.

payroll-bot: Reminder: for UK employees include EMPID, NI number (last 4 only in ticket), and "INTERNATIONAL-TAX: UK" tag. Payroll will flag tax-team involvement automatically.

alex-se: thanks for helping — can the company provide an estimate of net retro before final approval? I want to make sure the tax hit isn't a surprise.

omar-comp: we'll provide a preliminary estimate in the payroll ticket. If Alex prefers, comp can run a gross-up quote (company covers additional tax) but that requires explicit approval.

zoe-peopleops: final notes for playbook update: 1) retro >30 days = Comp Director + Legal required; 2) UK employees: tax-team loop and consider gross-up; 3) use exception memo template above; 4) payroll ticket subject prefix = EXCEPTION-BACKPAY; 5) if Exec review required escalate via comp@redwood. Leaving thread open until ticket confirms inclusion in July run. :white_check_mark:
